rules.rule: Whether a property defines an attribute or blocks depends only on the schema: the same property is an attribute for one schema and a block for another
A body can be a JSON object, whose properties define its attributes and blocks
A body can be a JSON array of objects, whose properties are visited object by object, in order, as if they were in one object; an empty array is an empty body
An element of a body array that isn't an object, such as a string, null or an array, is an error
Dynamic attributes processing needs a single JSON object: a body that is an array of objects, or the null that a null element of a block array gives, is an error in that mode
Dynamic attributes processing gives an attribute for each property of the body object, whatever its value, named as written, and no blocks, and a property defined twice is an error
In dynamic attributes processing, property names that differ only in Unicode normalization are different attributes (disputed)
A property named // in a body is ignored, whatever its value and however its name is escaped, in exhaustive, partial and dynamic attributes processing and in block bodies and body arrays
A schema that requests an attribute or block type named // gets the property named // (disputed)
A property named // at a block's label level is a label, because a label level isn't a body
An attribute the schema requests is defined by the property with its name, whose value is the attribute's expression
An attribute that isn't required and has no property is absent from the body content
A required attribute without a property is an error, also in partial processing and in a body array, and an attribute whose value is null is present
An attribute defined by two properties is an error, in exhaustive and partial processing, across the objects of a body array, and when one name is escaped
In exhaustive processing, a property that the schema requests neither as an attribute nor as a block type is an error

Partial processing puts the properties the schema doesn't request into a new body, leaving out the requested attributes and every property of a requested block type; that body can be processed in any mode, and a property defined twice is an error only when later processing takes it as an attribute
Partial processing followed by exhaustive processing of the remaining body gives the same attributes, blocks and errors as one exhaustive pass with both schemas
For a block type without labels, an object value defines one block whose body is that object
For a block type without labels, an array of objects defines a block for each object, in order, and an empty array defines none
A block type's property repeated in one body defines blocks for every definition, in order, interleaved with other block types
A block type's property whose value is a string, number or boolean is an error, and so is an array element that is a string or number
A null where a block body or array of block bodies is expected defines no block, and a null element of a block array defines a block with an empty body when the body is processed by schema (disputed)
An array element of a block array defines one block whose body is that array of objects, when the body is processed by schema (disputed)
Each label of a block type is one nested level of object properties, whose names are the label values, before the block body
Several properties at a label level, including a repeated property, define blocks for each, in order
A label level can be an array of objects, whose properties are visited in order, and after the labels an array of objects defines several blocks with the same labels

A label level that is a string, number, null or array of non-objects is an error, and so is a string or number where a block body follows the labels, including when a block has fewer label levels than its type has labels
A label level with no properties, an empty object or an empty array, is an error (disputed)
Each block's body is processed with the schema for its block type, recursively, and an error in a nested body is an error
A schema that requests an attribute and a block type with the same name is not an error, and the property defines the attribute (disputed)
A schema that requests the same attribute twice, optional or required, is not an error for the JSON syntax (disputed)
Dynamic attributes processing of the body that partial processing leaves from a body array is an error, because that body is still the array (disputed)
A property that partial processing took as an attribute isn't a block when a later schema asks for a block type of that name (disputed)
